The stall watchdog waits by polling: every --poll-sec (default 60 s) it checks the --path set for any file newer than the last activity; it exits 4 when --cap-min (default 90) passes, exits 3 after --stale-min (default 20) minutes with no change, exits 2 on a usage error, and never exits 0.

The wake is the exit of a background shell: the orchestrator starts the watchdog in the spawn's own message, reads the child's output tail on fire, re-arms if it still produces or stops the child and parks if silent, and kills the watchdog on normal completion.

Whether a background job's exit actually re-invokes an idle agent on each harness is not shown by this repository: no conformance probe covers it and PARITY.md records stall-watchdog.sh as not proven; only a live run per harness settles it.
